name: knownote
description: A local-first knowledge note-taking tool that transforms your PDFs, documents, and web pages into a queryable, citable, and traceable personal knowledge base using RAG technology
author: MrSibe

scripts.typecheck: npm run typecheck:node && npm run typecheck:web && npm run typecheck:test

//test: `node --test` strips TypeScript types rather than compiling them, and strip-only
mode rejects the enums the production sources use (src/shared/utils/logger.ts is
on every loader's import path). `--experimental-transform-types` lets those
modules load unmodified, so parser tests can import the real loaders instead of
//dependencies: ONLY packages that cannot be bundled belong here.
electron-vite defaults build.externalizeDeps to true, so every `dependencies`
entry stays a runtime `require()` in out/main and out/preload. Those imports
must exist inside app.asar, and electron-builder's node-module collector is
what puts them there. Keeping this list tiny is the point.
KnowNote uses npm, not pnpm, because that collector is built around npm's
node_modules layout. Under pnpm's virtual store it silently dropped transitive
dependencies (jsdom -> whatwg-url -> tr46, http-proxy-agent -> debug -> ms) and
v1.2.1 shipped an app.asar that crashed with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Hand-listing
those transitives here was the old workaround; do not reintroduce it. Instead
keep this list minimal and rely on `allowMissingDependencies: false` in
electron-builder.yml, which fails the build if collection ever misses a
production dependency instead of shipping a broken app.
1. better-sqlite3, sqlite-vec - native addons; rollup cannot inline .node or
.dylib. Also listed in asarUnpack so they stay loadable from disk.
2. jsdom - rollup's commonjs plugin cannot parse a generated file inside its
cssstyle dependency (the source is valid JS, `node --check` accepts it), so
jsdom cannot be bundled and its whole subtree has to be collected intact.
3. @mixmark-io/domino - turndown calls require('@mixmark-io/domino') while its
module body runs, which rollup leaves as a runtime require. It has zero
dependencies, so collecting it is trivially safe.
4. anki-apkg-export - its dist branches on `typeof window` to choose between
require('script-loader!sql.js') (a webpack-only loader prefix) and a plain
require('sql.js'). Inlining it makes rollup hoist that dead browser require
to the top of the bundle, so the packaged app dies at startup with
`Cannot find module 'script-loader!sql.js'`. Keeping it external lets the
packaged copy run its real Node branch instead.
5. pdfjs-dist - its Node branch polyfills DOMMatrix/ImageData/Path2D by
`createRequire(import.meta.url)`-ing its optional dependency
@napi-rs/canvas, and then runs `new DOMMatrix()` at module scope. Bundling
it keeps the polyfill from finding that package, and because pdfjs-dist was
a devDependency the package was never shipped either, so the main process
died with `ReferenceError: DOMMatrix is not defined`. External makes pdfjs
resolve its own optional native peer normally; @napi-rs/canvas and its
platform binary are collected as ordinary production dependencies and the
.node is unpacked by asarUnpack.
6. @huggingface/transformers - the built-in local embedding backend loads it
at runtime for ONNX inference. It brings native onnxruntime-node (and, via
its module-load-time `import sharp`, sharp's platform packages), which
rollup cannot inline. Keeping it external lets the node build resolve its
own native deps. onnxruntime-node and sharp are also listed here directly
because they are runtime-resolved natives rather than code we bundle, and
both are in asarUnpack so they are loadable from disk.
Everything else lives in devDependencies and is bundled into out/main by rollup.
//devDependencies: Everything else, including packages the main process uses. electron-vite
bundles devDependencies into out/main and out/renderer, and electron-builder
excludes devDependencies from the package, so these end up in the bundle
